chunks: He said: al-Mudhaffar ibn Muhammad al-Balkhi reported to me, he said: Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Hammam al-Iskafi narrated to us, he said: Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Ma Bandar reported to me, from Mansoor ibn al-Abbas al-Qasbani who narrated to them from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Khazzaz, from Ali ibn Uqbah, from Salim ibn Abu Hafsah, who said:

When Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, peace be upon them both, passed away, I said to my companions: Wait for me until I visit Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, to offer my condolences. So I entered upon him and offered my condolences, then I said: "Indeed we belong to God and to Him we shall return. By God, gone is the one who used to say: 'The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, said' without being asked about who stood between him and the Messenger of God. No, by God, his like shall never be seen again."

He said: Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, remained silent for a while, then said: "God, the Mighty and Majestic, said: Indeed among My servants is one who gives in charity a piece of a date, and I nurture it for him just as one of you nurtures his foal, until I make it for him like the mountain of Uhud."

So I went out to my companions and said: "I have never seen anything more astonishing than this! We used to think highly of Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, saying: 'The Messenger of God said' without intermediary, but Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, said to me: 'God, the Mighty and Majestic, said' without intermediary!"

key_terms.فلوّه: His foal (young horse); metaphor for nurturing and growth
key_terms.واسطة: Intermediary; the chain of narrators between the Imam and the ultimate source
key_terms.يتصدق بشق تمرة: Gives in charity a piece of a date; illustrates that even the smallest charity is immensely rewarded

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq narrate directly from God without intermediary?
ai.summary: Salim ibn Abu Hafsah recounts his visit to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) after the passing of Imam al-Baqir (AS). While praising al-Baqir for narrating directly from the Prophet without intermediaries, Imam al-Sadiq responded by quoting directly from God regarding the reward of charity, astonishing Salim who realized that al-Sadiq's station surpassed even his father's. This hadith illustrates the Shia belief in the Imams' direct divine connection and the transfer of authority from one Imam to the next.
